summary: A first-person narrator from Cory Doctorow's Little Brother-style fiction (labeled Book 1, part 95) recounts a night after a setback where he and Ange march a bag of smashed electronics to the sea to soak it in salt water. On the dark, slippery rocks Ange catches him, and they share a wordless, spiritual moment without kissing. The narrator then plans to sign and publish his keys to start a web of trust, and the passage ends with the group riding Muni, where Xnetters clone transit passes to ride anonymously.
one_line: The narrator and Ange soak smashed electronics in the sea at night, share a charged silent moment, then ride Muni on cloned passes.
key_facts: The narrator marches a bag of smashed electronics down to the sea to soak it in salt water for ten minutes.
Ange takes the narrator's arm and says "That was beautiful" in his ear before they walk to the sea together.
It was perfectly dark by the sea, and the rocks were slippery and sharp, with the group using keychain lights.
The bag of smashed electronics weighed about six pounds.
Ange catches the narrator with a surprisingly strong grip when he slips and keeps him upright.
The narrator says he could smell Ange's perfume, which smelled like new cars.
Ange wears mannish, black-rimmed glasses that magnify her big eyes.
The narrator had kissed a total of three girls in his life before this night.
The narrator did not kiss Ange or take her hand; they shared a moment he describes as spiritual.
The narrator has a lot of typing to do that night, putting keys onto his keychain, signing them and publishing the signed keys.
The narrator's plan of signing and publishing keys is described as starting the web of trust.
Jolu waited for his brother's friend to come pick up his coolers.
The group walked up the road to the nearest Muni stop and boarded a train or bus.
None of the group used an issued Muni pass.
Xnetters habitually cloned someone else's Muni pass three or four times a day, assuming a new identity for every ride.
